CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Close Phase One now. Commit to additional U.S. farm purchases—soy, pork, and related products we already need after African swine fever—in exchange for cancellation of the 15 December List 4B tariffs and a simultaneous, phased rollback of some existing duties (at minimum the 1 September List 4A tranche). Do not fire the unreliable-entity list or new rare-earth restrictions while the text is being papered, and do not blow up the deal over Huawei, which Washington has already kept off this package. The purchase commitment is the price of taking the December consumer-electronics tariff off the table; it is not a structural surrender.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not existential. U.S. customs imports from China have fallen from $41.2bn in July to $33.4bn in December (−19%), List 3 is already at 25%, List 4A at 15% has been in force since 1 September, and Huawei plus affiliates remain on the Entity List with Google/GMS and U.S. chip suppliers cut off since mid-May—firm-level targeting of our national champion that Phase One still does not unwind. Q3 growth printed a record-low 6.0%, August industrial production slowed to 4.4% y/y, and pork-driven CPI has climbed through the autumn (index 108.1 in July to 111.2 by December). Oxford Economics warned that if the 15 December tranche on phones, laptops and toys proceeds, 2020 growth could sink toward 5.5%. That is the +0.4 reading: major export-sector and tech-self-sufficiency damage, not a reserves or financial-stability break (FX reserves are stable near $3.13tn; the yuan has settled around 7.03 after the August break of 7 and the manipulator designation).

The same evidence argues against escalation and for a contingent purchase close. Talks are already advanced: on 11 October Trump announced a Phase One in principle ($40–50bn annual ag buys, IP and currency language, mid-October hike delayed). Gao Feng stated as recently as 5 December that a Phase One deal requires tariffs to be lowered accordingly, and both sides were reported close on the size of relief with farm-purchase guarantees and which lists to roll back still open. China already signaled goodwill in mid-September (16-category exemption list; soy and pork carved out of extra retaliation). Buying U.S. pork and soy is also a domestic-inflation hedge, not a pure giveaway. Escalating now would likely trigger List 4B and invite further entity-list or Hong Kong-linked measures after Washington signed the Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act; holding without a purchase-for-relief package leaves the 15 December cliff live. Concede purchases against a matching U.S. offer (Dec-15 cancellation plus some existing-tariff rollback); leave Huawei, SOE subsidies and cybersecurity for later phases.
key_factors: Dec 15 List 4B (~$156bn phones/laptops/toys) still live three days out
US imports from China down ~19% Jul–Dec; List 3 at 25% and List 4A at 15% already in force
Huawei Entity List plus Android/chip cutoff remains outside Phase One
Phase One in principle (11 Oct) with farm purchases and IP/currency chapters; Gao Feng still conditioning a deal on tariff cuts (5 Dec)
China Q3 GDP 6.0% record low, pork CPI pressure, but reserves stable and IP recovered into year-end
Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act signed late Nov briefly stalled talks; do not add a second front

sources_cited.excerpt: After Washington talks, Trump announces a "Phase One" deal in principle: China to buy roughly $40–50B of US agricultural products annually; IP and currency issues also cited. Planned mid-October tariff hike delayed.
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
USTR splits List 4: List 4A effective Sept 1; List 4B (including many cell phones, laptops, toys, apparel items) delayed to Dec 15.
List 4A takes effect at 15% (~$110–125B of Chinese imports). China's first tranche of the ~$75B retaliation also takes effect.
US imports from China fell from $41.2bn (Jul) to $33.4bn (Dec), −19% over the window.
China reserves excluding gold stable near $3.13tn through Dec 2019 — no FX-crisis signal.
China CPI index rose from 108.1 (Jul) to 111.2 (Dec), consistent with pork-driven inflation.
Gao Feng, 5 Dec 2019: if the two sides reach a phase one deal, tariffs should be lowered accordingly; core issues still under discussion.
Bloomberg (~4 Dec): US negotiators expect Phase One completed before 15 Dec tariffs; outstanding issues are farm-purchase guarantees and which tariffs to roll back.
Q3 GDP 6.0% lowest on record; Oxford Economics: Dec 15 tariffs on consumer electronics could push 2020 growth toward 5.5%.
